tools.name: Claude Code
used_for: translation of the challenge text into Malay
comparison with other public entries to this challenge and, from it, features built by several SI sessions in parallel (15 November 2026)
red-team review of the entry against the aim of a Global Award, its measurements, and the changes the author adopted from it (15 November 2026)
Indonesian and Malay translations of the interface (optional; English is the default and the reference), not reviewed by a native speaker

further additions on the night of 15 November 2026, proposed and built by SI sessions in parallel after reading other public entries: more candidate regions, own-coordinate terrain, eclipses, a visual pass, validation at scale
English text, drafted from the author's choices and the measured results, reviewed by the author

decided_by_author: audiences: mission planners, educators, the public (all three named in the challenge)
items to build: all twelve items that SI listed from the challenge text (its 'Your solution may include' list and its 'Potential Considerations')
project name: suggested by SI, chosen by the author

further options from the challenge text (sequential comparison, an educational game, terrain for custom coordinates, slopes and shadow conditions on the map): chosen by the author, all four, on 15 November 2026 from NASA's own wording, listed by SI

further features suggested by SI (mission window finder, shareable links with a plain verdict and a Now button, a page for teachers, a guided tour built as one button that opens the one-kilometre example; then a real NASA photograph on the first screen, a one-year overview of every listed site, Indonesian and Malay interface options): suggested by SI at the author's request on 15 November 2026; the author considered each list and chose all of them

the aim of a Global Award, and which changes to adopt from an SI red-team review of the entry (15 November 2026): the NASA PGDA comparison over the same 18.6 years with a sensitivity test at the ridge check point; a 360-degree horizon strip and a one-line verdict at the top of every card; the terrain range on the terrain cards; four more south polar sites (three future targets picked by SI from NASA and LROC pages that state a coordinate, and the place where IM-1 came to rest)

features that other public entries to this challenge had (15 November 2026): ready-made comparisons with an opening sentence about rescheduling, a mission check with a GO / RISKY / NO-GO line, a calendar of every site by day, a view from the lander, dates to the end of 2030; asked for by the author, built by SI

the instruction to close the gaps to other public entries (night of 15 November 2026): SI chose and built four more Artemis III candidate regions, a terrain skyline for own coordinates south of 75 degrees south, lunar eclipses with an example battery size and ground stations, a visual pass with one header and footer, a JPL Horizons check at scale, a CSV download and a guided tour; the author approved the plan and had not reviewed the result line by line when the build was published
